correctness.rationale: For even L, N=product(aj-1) is 1 mod a; b is -1 mod a. Any solution N=ax+by forces y=aj-1 with 1<=j<=L via by<=N and b>N/(aL). This y divides N, is coprime to a, and hence divides x; it is >=2. Thus every solution has gcd>1. The chosen b is within a above N/(aL), yielding g(a,b)/b>=aL/(1+a^2 L/N). Since N>=(a-1)^L, the ratio diverges and b tends to infinity. The endpoint a=1,2 follows exactly from credited Jaffe Propositions 5.1–5.2. The standalone stdlib checker confirms 77 finite parameter pairs and 616 ordinary nonprimitive representations; the proof covers all parameters.

value.rationale: A natural structural gap after existing formulas for a=1,2 is the effect of fixing one generator and varying the other. The result provides a sharp yes/no dichotomy, with a systematic product construction that forces all possible ordinary representations to be nonprimitive. It invalidates any uniform linear-in-b extrapolation for all fixed a>=3; this is a meaningful infinite parameter-growth boundary, not a table recomputation or arbitrary slice. It does not claim exact g or density over all b.
